headline: Fifty-three times out of fifty-nine, a seller was given someone else's name
standfirst: An owner thinking about selling asks ChatGPT who to use. It gives them one answer, a name, and they ring it. Nobody rings you to tell you it happened. On 6 August we asked 59 times and checked what came back.
question: "Who are the best business brokers in Melbourne?"
counts: 6 of 59
sampled answers named Trident Business Sales.
the positions you held when named. When you appear, you appear near the top.
answers did not mention you at all.
finding_label: And when we asked about you by name
finding:
We asked the assistants directly about Trident, on 6 and 7 August.

The answers were not consistent with each other, and one of them raised material about your firm that we are not going to put in writing to you or to anyone else.

It is not defamatory of us to say it exists, and it is not something you can currently see. It is the first thing we would want to show you on a call, privately, with the screen in front of you.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 59 times on 6 August 2026, named: LINK Business Brokers, Benchmark Business Sales, Xcllusive Business Sales, Aussie Business Sales, VIC Brokers, Morgan Business Sales, Business Brokers Victoria, Finn Business Sales.
why_matters: Forty years of reputation in this trade, and in fifty-three conversations out of fifty-nine your name did not come up at all. When it did, you ranked first or second. So reach is one issue. What is being said when you are found is a separate one, and it is the more urgent of the two.

headline: AI does not think Buyers Advocate is a company
standfirst: A buyer ready to spend asks ChatGPT who to use. It gives them one answer, a name, and they ring it. There is no page two. On 6 August we asked 35 times and checked what came back.
question: "Who are the best buyers advocates in Melbourne?"
counts: sampled answers used your website as a source. More than any other website in the study, including every competitor and every industry body.
5 of 8
times we asked who Buyers Advocate is, the machines answered that they did not know.
competitors named in its place, in a single live answer on 7 August.
finding_label: What it said, word for word
finding:
We asked Claude directly who you are. Its opening sentence:

"'Buyers Advocate' isn't one specific company here. It's the general term Melbourne buyer's agents use to describe the role."

It then named seven Melbourne firms that use the phrase, recommended REBAA's directory as the place to find a good one, and did not name you at any point.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 35 times on 6 August 2026, named: Cate Bakos Property, Property Mavens, Davidson Property Advocates, Property Home Base, Wakelin Property Advisory, BuyerX, National Property Buyers, Parker Buyer Advocates.
why_matters: Your website is the single most-quoted source in this category, and the machine reading it has concluded you are a job title rather than a business. Your content is being used to introduce buyers to seven of your competitors. That is not a ranking problem and no amount of content fixes it, because the machine is not failing to rank you. It is failing to see that you exist.

headline: AI has given Mercury a leadership structure you never published
standfirst: An owner thinking about selling asks ChatGPT who to use, and rings the name it gives. On 6 August we asked 59 times, and you did better than most. This is about what is said once you are found.
question: "Who are the best business brokers in Melbourne?"

your position on the ChatGPT app, in a shortlist of eight.
finding:
Asked about Mercury, the assistants supplied a full leadership structure: who founded the firm, who is senior, who reports to whom.

Your people are real and correctly named. Your website gives none of them a job title.

So the hierarchy a prospective seller is being told about your firm did not come from you. Separately, two runs on the same afternoon gave two different ABNs for your business.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 59 times on 6 August 2026, also named: LINK Business Brokers, Benchmark Business Sales, Xcllusive Business Sales, Aussie Business Sales, VIC Brokers, Morgan Business Sales, Trident Business Sales.
why_matters: You are being found, which puts you ahead of most of the firms we screened. But someone selling a business they have built for twenty years wants to know exactly who will handle it. Right now that answer is being written by something other than you, and it has already invented one detail we can show you.

headline: AI added a person to your team who does not exist
standfirst: An owner thinking about selling asks ChatGPT who to use, and rings the name it gives. On 6 August we asked 59 times and checked what came back.
question: "Who are the best business brokers in Melbourne?"
counts: 0 of 59
sampled answers named Expert Business Brokers.
4 of 59
answers used your website as a source.
finding:
Asked directly about your firm, one assistant listed six people on your team.

Five of them are yours. The sixth does not exist, and never has.

The invented name sat in the same sentence, in the same confident tone, as the five real ones. Nothing in the answer distinguished them, and a seller reading it has no way to tell which is which.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 59 times on 6 August 2026, named: LINK Business Brokers, Benchmark Business Sales, Xcllusive Business Sales, Aussie Business Sales, VIC Brokers, Morgan Business Sales, Trident Business Sales, Finn Business Sales.
why_matters: That is the part worth sitting with. The machine was right five times out of six, in one breath, with no change in tone. Confidence is not evidence of accuracy, and your buyers have no way to tell the difference. Neither did we, until we checked.

headline: Metropole Melbourne did not come up. Not once in thirty-five answers.
standfirst: A buyer ready to spend asks ChatGPT or Claude who to use. It gives them one answer, a name, and they ring it. There is no page two. On 6 August we asked 35 times, in fresh sessions, from Melbourne.
question: "Who are the best buyers advocates in Melbourne?"
counts: 0 of 35

0 of 35

0 of 35

finding_label: And here is the part that should bother you
finding:
We then asked the same machines about Metropole by name. They answered accurately and in detail: the founding year, the offices, your Brighton address correct to the street number, and nine of your people by name and role.

So they are not missing information about you. They have it, and it is right.

They simply never reach for it when somebody is asking who to use.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 35 times on 6 August 2026, named: Cate Bakos Property, Property Mavens, Property Home Base, Wakelin Property Advisory, BuyerX, National Property Buyers, Davidson Property Advocates, Empower Wealth.
why_matters: You have spent decades building one of the largest content operations in Australian property. That work is in the machines. It is accurate. And in thirty-five attempts it did not once turn into a recommendation. Being known and being chosen are two different things, and only one of them books a client.

headline: The machines are reading your site and cannot tell that it is yours
standfirst: A buyer ready to spend asks ChatGPT who to use, and rings the name it gives. There is no page two. On 6 August we asked 35 times and checked what came back.
question: "Who are the best buyers advocates in Melbourne?"
counts: 9 of 35
sampled answers used your website as a source.
answers named you as a recommended firm that we could attribute to you with confidence.
finding_label: The problem, and it is not carelessness on your part
finding:
Your business name is also the phrase every buyer types. When an assistant writes those three words, neither a reader nor the machine can tell whether it means your firm or the whole category.

We can show you this precisely. A competing Melbourne firm carries your exact business name as the title of its homepage.

Two different businesses, one string. In the sampled answers, facts about each appeared under wording that could have described either.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 35 times on 6 August 2026, named: Cate Bakos Property, Property Mavens, Concierge Buyers Advocates, Property Home Base, Wakelin Property Advisory, BuyerX, National Property Buyers.
why_matters: Your content is being read nine times in thirty-five and is not reliably being attached to you. Every enquiry that starts in an AI answer is invisible in your funnel: no impression, no click, no record, just a buyer you never met. The name that once helped you be found is now the reason you cannot be identified.

headline: You won ten of thirty-five. Someone else won the other twenty-five.
standfirst: A buyer ready to spend asks ChatGPT who to use. It gives them one answer, a name, and they ring it. On 6 August we asked 35 times, and you performed better than anyone else we screened. This is about the gap.
question: "Who are the best buyers advocates in Melbourne?"
counts: sampled answers named Cate Bakos Property. More than any other firm in the study.
times you were listed first.
answers did not name you at all. Same question, same day, fresh session each time.
finding:
Your details came back right. Your team names were correct. We would rather tell you that than invent a problem.

But twenty-five times out of thirty-five, a buyer asking the single most valuable question in your category was handed somebody else's name.

Not because anything is wrong. Because the machine chose differently that time, and nothing you can see tells you when or why.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 35 times on 6 August 2026, also named: Property Mavens, Davidson Property Advocates, Property Home Base, Wakelin Property Advisory, BuyerX, National Property Buyers, Parker Buyer Advocates.
why_matters: You are the most visible buyer's advocate in Melbourne and you are still absent from seven answers in ten. Every other line in your marketing has a before and an after. This one does not. You have the most to lose here precisely because you are currently winning, and you would be the last to know if that moved.

headline: Twenty-eight times out of thirty-five, a buyer was given someone else's name
standfirst: A buyer ready to spend asks ChatGPT who to use, and rings the name it gives. There is no page two. On 6 August we asked 35 times, and for a firm with no shopfront you did respectably.
question: "Who are the best buyers advocates in Melbourne?"
counts: 7 of 35
sampled answers named Concierge Buyers Advocates, at positions 4 and 7.
9 of 35
answers used your website as a source.
answers named somebody else and not you.
finding_label: And something you should know about
finding:
Your website does not name a principal and does not publish an address. When we asked the machines who runs Concierge, they answered anyway.

They produced a founder, a founding year, staff first names, and two performance figures.

Some of it is right. We checked. But none of it came from you, because you publish none of it. The account of who you are, being read to buyers today, was assembled entirely by other people.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 35 times on 6 August 2026, also named: Cate Bakos Property, Property Mavens, Property Home Base, Wakelin Property Advisory, BuyerX, National Property Buyers, Davidson Property Advocates.
why_matters: You built a flat-fee, no-storefront model deliberately, and it works. But it has left the machines to write your introduction for you, from sources you did not choose and cannot see. Four times in five, the buyer heard a competitor's name instead of yours, and nobody rang to tell you.

headline: Fifty-five times out of fifty-nine, a seller was given someone else's name
standfirst: An owner thinking about selling asks ChatGPT who to use, and rings the name it gives. Nobody rings you to tell you it happened. On 6 August we asked 59 times, in fresh sessions, from Melbourne.
question: "Who are the best business brokers in Melbourne?"
counts: 4 of 59
sampled answers named Lloyds Business Brokers.
the positions you held when named. High when you are there.
answers did not mention you at all.
finding_label: And one thing it told us about itself
finding:
Asked directly about Lloyds, one assistant placed your Managing Director in the wrong state.

Another named nobody at all, and said plainly that it was working from your company name rather than from anything it actually knew about the firm.

That second answer is the more useful one. It is the machine admitting it is producing something plausible rather than something known. A seller reading the polished version never sees that line.
named_instead: ChatGPT and Claude, sampled 59 times on 6 August 2026, named: LINK Business Brokers, Benchmark Business Sales, Xcllusive Business Sales, Aussie Business Sales, VIC Brokers, Morgan Business Sales, Trident Business Sales.
why_matters: Forty years in corporate sales, and in fifty-five conversations out of fifty-nine your name did not come up. When it did, you ranked second. So this is not a quality problem, it is a reach problem, and it is happening in a channel where you have no impressions, no clicks and no record to look at.
